title: Scientific bases for precompetition tapering strategies (Mujika & Padilla, 2003)
publisher: PubMed / Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise
claims: A taper is a progressive, non-linear reduction of training load intended to reduce accumulated fatigue without compromising adaptations.
The taper should maintain training intensity, reduce training volume by up to 60-90%, and slightly reduce training frequency by no more than 20%.
Optimal taper duration ranges from 4 to more than 28 days, and progressive non-linear tapers outperform step tapers.
Performance usually improves by about 3%, with a typical range of 0.5-6.0%, across cardiorespiratory, metabolic, hematological, hormonal, neuromuscular and psychological status.
